name: Kundapura Koli Saaru
instructions: 1. Roast the coriander, cumin, mustard, fenugreek, peppercorns, cinnamon, cloves, mace, and dried chillies in a little oil until fragrant, then grind with grated coconut and tamarind into a smooth paste.
2. Heat coconut oil in a heavy-bottomed pan, sauté onions and curry leaves until golden.
3. Add the chicken pieces and turmeric powder, cooking until the chicken turns opaque.
4. Pour in the prepared ground masala paste and enough water to reach desired consistency.
5. Simmer on low heat until the chicken is tender and the oil separates from the gravy.
6. Adjust salt and serve hot with neer dosa or steamed rice.
description: Originating from the Kundapura region in the Udupi district of coastal Karnataka, this dish is a quintessential Bunt community delicacy. It is famous for its bold, spicy profile and the unique use of coconut oil and roasted spices, making it a comfort food staple at local weddings and celebrations.
